```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
options(digits = 5, width = 95)
```

Most chamber users (upland soils, upland tree stems) never meet ebullition and
never need this vignette: the core path of `stemflux`
(`goFlux -> best.flux -> flag_detection -> qc_screens`, wrapped by
`process_fluxes()`) does not call any of the code below. Over water, saturated
peat or flooded stems, bubbles add abrupt step-ups to the smooth diffusive
rise, and one linear or Hutchinson-Mosier fit through both components gives a
number that is neither. This add-on is switched on with a single argument,
`process_fluxes(ebullition = "flag" | "split")`, or used directly through
`detect_ebullition()`, `split_ebullition()` and `merge_ebullition()`.

## A real closure with bubbles

Example `e` of `stemflux_examples()` is a real 276 s floating-chamber closure
on open water at site CP40 (Christian Point, a ghost-forest mangrove site) of
the NASA BlueFlux campaign (ABB/LGR GLA131, "LGR2"). Geometry: Area 324.3 cm2,
Vtot 4.318 L, Tcham 28.7 C (site-day mean air temperature), Pcham 101.325
kPa. We put it next to the clean tree-stem closure `a` for comparison.

What the trace shows, checked against the campaign's own segmentation
(`output/ebullition/placements_summary.csv`, `all_traces.rds`): CH4 rises
diffusively from the first sample (about 11 ppb s-1) while CO2 rises cleanly
from t = 0, so the chamber was already sealed when this window starts (the
placement overlaps the campaign's processed flux `44857_CP40_Water_78`). At
42-46 s the CH4 jumps by about 675 ppb in five consecutive 1 Hz samples
(112-160 ppb each), then resumes a steady rise to 4600 ppb. The campaign
script, which tests single samples against a 100 ppb step, recorded those
five samples as "5 jumps". They are one bubble burst, not five bubbles and
not the closure onset; stemflux merges consecutive flagged samples into one
event by default (`merge.consecutive = TRUE`). No closure in the campaign's
archive shows several isolated steps on a clean baseline (all its flagged
traces are bursts of consecutive samples), which is why this one is shipped.

```{r make}
library(stemflux)
ex <- stemflux_examples(c("a", "e"))
both <- ex$data
ex$aux[, c("example", "UniqueID", "obs.length", "Area", "Vtot", "Tcham")]
e <- both[both$UniqueID == "BF_CP40_2022-10-23_P06", ]
```

## Step 1: detect events

`detect_ebullition()` works on the flagged rows of each `UniqueID`. The
default method follows Hoffmann et al. (2017): the point-to-point changes are
compared with quartile fences `Q3 + k * IQR`; stemflux's default `k = 3` keeps
Gaussian noise below the fence on 600-point closures (`k = 0.25` reproduces
Hoffmann's own fences, which were used to select fitting windows rather than
to sum bubbles). Detected events are overlaid on the trace. On this closure
the IQR fences (threshold about 17 ppb per sample, set by the closure's own
noise) also catch the shoulders of the burst, so the merged event carries
about 1100 ppb; the campaign's fixed 100 ppb criterion gives 676 ppb in five
samples (shown last).

```{r detect, fig.height = 5}
eb <- detect_ebullition(both, "CH4dry_ppb", method = "iqr")
eb$summary[, c("UniqueID", "n_points", "n_events", "total_ebullitive", "total_rise",
               "ebullitive_fraction", "threshold_used")]
eb$events
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
plot(e$Etime, e$CH4dry_ppb, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, type = "b", xlab = "seconds since window start",
     ylab = "CH4 (ppb)", main = "BlueFlux CP40, 2022-10-23: diffusive rise with one bubble burst (red)")
ev <- eb$events[eb$events$UniqueID == "BF_CP40_2022-10-23_P06", ]
tr <- eb$trace[eb$trace$UniqueID == "BF_CP40_2022-10-23_P06", ]
points(tr$Etime_eb[tr$is_outlier], tr$CH4dry_ppb[tr$is_outlier], col = "red", pch = 16, cex = 0.9)
abline(v = ev$Etime, col = "red", lty = 2)
text(ev$Etime, max(e$CH4dry_ppb), sprintf("event: +%.0f ppb", ev$dC), pos = 4, col = "red", cex = 0.8)
plot(e$Etime, e$CO2dry_ppm, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, type = "b", xlab = "seconds since window start",
     ylab = "CO2 (ppm)", main = "CO2 rises from t = 0: the chamber was sealed before the burst")
abline(v = ev$Etime, col = "red", lty = 2)
par(op)
camp <- detect_ebullition(both, "CH4dry_ppb", method = "threshold", jump.thresh = 100, merge.consecutive = FALSE)
camp$summary[camp$summary$UniqueID == "BF_CP40_2022-10-23_P06", c("n_events", "total_ebullitive")]   # the campaign's count
```

Two alternatives are available: `method = "threshold"` (a fixed jump size in
gas units, the criterion used in the BlueFlux processing) and
`method = "runvar"` (running variance of the changes above a cutoff, after the
description of So et al. 2024).

```{r alt}
detect_ebullition(both, "CH4dry_ppb", method = "threshold", jump.thresh = 40)$summary$n_events
detect_ebullition(both, "CH4dry_ppb", method = "runvar", runvar_window = 5, runvar_cutoff = 30)$summary$n_events
```

## Step 2: split into a de-ebulliated goFlux input and an ebullitive flux

```{r split}
sp <- split_ebullition(eb)
sp$ebullitive
plot(sp$diffusive$Etime, sp$diffusive$CH4dry_ppb_raw, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = "grey70",
     xlab = "Etime (s)", ylab = "CH4 (ppb)", main = "raw (grey) and de-ebulliated (black; red = buffer, flag 0)")
points(sp$diffusive$Etime, sp$diffusive$CH4dry_ppb, pch = 16, cex = 0.4,
       col = ifelse(sp$diffusive$flag == 1, "black", "red"))
```

`sp$diffusive` has goFlux's shape: the gas column now holds the de-ebulliated
trace, the raw values are kept in `CH4dry_ppb_raw`, and the equilibration
buffer around each event has `flag = 0`, so goFlux ignores it. (The clean
closure `a` is untouched: no events, all rows keep `flag = 1`.)

## Step 3: diffusive term with goFlux, then merge

```{r goflux}
invisible(capture.output({
  diff_res <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::goFlux(sp$diffusive, "CH4dry_ppb"))
}))
diff_best <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::best.flux(diff_res))
out <- merge_ebullition(diff_best, sp$ebullitive)
out[, c("UniqueID", "best.flux", "model", "flux_ebullitive", "flux_total", "n_events", "ebullitive_fraction")]
```

For the BlueFlux closure the ebullitive term is the summed bubble mass
divided by the closure duration, converted with that chamber's `flux.term`;
`ebullitive_fraction` says how much of the total came from bubbles. (The
campaign's own processing counted 5 single-sample jumps totalling 676 ppb in
this closure; `method = "threshold", jump.thresh = 100, merge.consecutive =
FALSE` reproduces that count exactly.)

## The same through `process_fluxes()`

The add-on is an option of the pipeline, not a separate path. `"flag"` fits
the whole trace but records the events; `"split"` fits the diffusive term on
the de-ebulliated trace. Per-closure control comes from `ebullition_ids` or a
logical `ebullition` column in the auxfile, so flooded stems can be split
while upland stems in the same call run the core path.

```{r process}
aux <- data.frame(UniqueID = c("2021-05-18_5086_I_7.0", "BF_CP40_2022-10-23_P06"), ebullition = c(FALSE, TRUE))
invisible(capture.output(       # goFlux's progress bar is captured
  res <- suppressWarnings(process_fluxes(both, aux = aux, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                       qc = list(c0 = TRUE, convex = TRUE),
                       ebullition = "split", ebullition_method = "iqr"))))
res
res$fluxes[, c("UniqueID", "qc_c0", "qc_convex", "qc_note")]
res$fluxes[, c("UniqueID", "ebullition_handling", "best.flux", "flux_diffusive", "flux_ebullitive",
               "flux_total", "n_ebullition_events", "MDF_emp", "det_class_emp")]
res$events
```

`write_outputs(res, dir)` then adds `ebullition_events.csv` next to
`fluxes.csv` and `settings.json`, and `settings.json` records
`ebullition`, `ebullition_method`, `ebullition_ids` and `ebullition_args`.

## How other packages handle ebullition

Checked in September 2026 from the sources or manuals named; "not verified"
marks claims that could not be checked.

| tool | ebullition / piecewise handling | verified from |
|---|---|---|
| goFlux 0.2.0 | none: one LM and one HM fit per closure, no mention of ebullition in the source tree | source snapshot |
| Hoffmann et al. 2017 (AMT 10:109-118), R script on Zenodo record 53168 | quartile fences `Q1 - 0.25 IQR`, `Q3 + 0.25 IQR` on the point-to-point changes; a moving-window linear fit is accepted only when all its changes lie inside the fences; diffusion from accepted windows, ebullition from the rest | script lines 365-366, 457-458 |
| `fluxCH4` (github.com/mthayne527/fluxCH4; standalone scripts) | GAM per id (diffusive if R2 > 0.99), otherwise GBMs via `dismo::gbm.step`; smoothed residuals, dynamic threshold (SD x multiplier) and a concentration-difference quantile test flag points; flagged points grouped into sequences (5-point buffer, minimum length) = events; floating chambers | README |
| So et al. 2024 (JGR-B, doi:10.1029/2024JG008035) | running variance above a user cutoff (about 0.5) defines event periods | the published description as relayed by the package author; code not verified |
| CRAN `flux` 0.3-0.1 (Jurasinski et al.; archived 2026-04-15) | `flux.odae()` fits all sub-models from n down to `min.allowed` points and keeps the best by nRMSE, i.e. it *excludes* rapid fluctuations/outliers to find stable linear conditions; nothing is quantified as ebullition | `flux.Rd` |
| `gasfluxes` 0.7-2 | linear, robust linear (MASS), HMR, NDFE; no ebullition or piecewise handling mentioned | CRAN manual |
| `HMR` 1.0.5 | prefiltering test classifies a series as 'Noise'; no ebullition handling | CRAN manual |
| `fluxfinder` 1.2.2 (Wilson et al. 2024, doi:10.1029/2024JG008208) | `ffi_fit_models()`, `ffi_hm()`, `ffi_qaqc()`; no ebullition or piecewise handling mentioned | CRAN manual |
| `RespChamberProc` (GitHub) | `changepoint`/`segmented` used to find the initial lag (breakpoint) of a closure, not ebullition | `R/fluxEstimates.R` |
| `FluxCalR` | no ebullition mention in the README; full source not inspected (not verified further) | README |

None of these packages is a dependency of stemflux; the survey is
documentation only.

## Provenance and citation etiquette

No code was copied from Hoffmann et al. (2017)'s Zenodo script (record 53168,
`R-Script-CH4_version_1.0.R`) or from the fluxCH4 repository. The `"iqr"`
method was re-implemented from the paper's description and then *checked*
against the script's fence definitions (lines 365-366 and 457-458 of that
script define `Q1 - Jumper*IQR` and `Q3 + Jumper*IQR` on `diff(y)` with
`Jumper = 0.25`); the per-closure application, the event-mass accounting and
the equilibration buffer are stemflux's own. The `"runvar"` method was written
from the published description of So et al. (2024) without access to their
code. The `"threshold"` method is stemflux's own. For the record: the Zenodo
record's license field reads "other-open" (open access, no standard license
named), and the fluxCH4 repository carries an MIT `LICENSE` file whose
copyright line is the unedited template ("First Last"); since nothing was
copied from either, neither license is exercised.

If you publish results obtained with the add-on, please cite the method
alongside goFlux and stemflux:

* `method = "iqr"`: Hoffmann, M., et al. (2017). Atmos. Meas. Tech. 10,
  109-118. doi:10.5194/amt-10-109-2017
* `method = "runvar"`: So, J. S., et al. (2024). J. Geophys. Res.
  Biogeosciences. doi:10.1029/2024JG008035
* goFlux: Rheault, K., Christiansen, J. R., & Larsen, K. S. (2024). JOSS
  9(96), 6393. doi:10.21105/joss.06393
* stemflux: `citation("stemflux")`

## Limitations

All three detectors are local tests. Slow bubble trains that raise the
concentration over many samples are missed by `"iqr"` and `"threshold"`;
analyzer artefacts (pressure transients, breaths on an inlet, valve switches)
look exactly like bubbles; and the ebullitive rate assumes the bubbles caught
in a 5-10 min closure represent the sampling period, which for episodic
ebullition is rarely true. Review `events` against the traces before
reporting, as was done by hand in the source campaign.
